spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates symbols() as the counter-style argument of counters() in generated content — the CSS Lists 3 counter-functions contract — with the exact declaration shown and applied via a constructed stylesheet.

interactive.rationale: System select, symbols input and separator input all re-render the outline live, regenerate the rule, and read the actual ::before content back with getComputedStyle instead of assuming.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises outline numbering in the document's own notation via counters()+symbols(), which is what the page builds.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported branch and the CSS.supports rejection branch are handled honestly, but an invalid positional combination (numeric/alphabetic with one symbol) silently returns the decimal branch whose message reads 'Plain decimal counters, for comparison' as if the user chose it.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5146996093616128 and CSS Lists 3 counter functions.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers parse-in-longhand/shorthand, all five systems, the positional two-symbol rule, counter()/counters() acceptance and a computed-style render check; on Chromium 141 the route honestly reports 1 pass / 7 fail because symbols() genuinely needs Chrome 154.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): exercised the system select through numeric and cyclic — each change re-rendered and reported 'This browser rejected symbols(...)' with the decimal fallback readout; console clean, no failed same-origin requests, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits an outline-numbered assert with style/usable/supported on every render.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, amber unsupported banner, focusable rule block, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: All three controls have real labels, the result readout is an aria-live output, the support banner is text with an aria-hidden icon, and the rule block is keyboard-focusable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); controls stack via auto-fit grid.

openQuestions.title: Explain the invalid positional combination instead of showing the comparison message
openQuestions.detail: counterStyle() returns null when numeric or alphabetic is chosen with fewer than two symbols, which routes the detail readout into the '(no symbols()) Plain decimal counters, for comparison' branch. A visitor who typed one symbol under 'numeric' is told they are looking at an intentional comparison rather than that their combination is invalid per the spec's positional-system rule. Add a distinct message ('numeric needs at least two symbols; showing decimal until you add one') mirroring the sibling system-explorer's per-card handling.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/css-symbols/counters-in-content/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp), where symbols() is genuinely unsupported (CSS.supports returns false — this browser predates Chrome 154). The page behaves exactly as the browser-version exception requires: an amber banner states the fallback, every control change re-renders and reports the rejection with the computed decimal read-back, and the Chrome 154 rule stays visible. Console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read with no overflow; feature /conformance/ honestly reported 1 pass / 7 fail on this build. One minor messaging gap around invalid positional input.
